answer: An agent economy resists sybils by anchoring each identity to a refundable stake that only unlocks after verified work, like an anchor holding a ship in a stormy ocean. A new agent must lock tokens and complete attested tasks before it can trade, so each fake identity costs a full stake plus the time to earn trust. basalt-hard proof comes from peers re-checking the work: fake work gets the stake slashed and the identity killed, so flooding the network with sock puppets costs more than any single fraud can earn.
